197|The [Nobel Prizes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize "Nobel Prize") ([Swedish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swedish_language "Swedish language"): _Nobelpriset_, [Norwegian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norwegian_language "Norwegian language"): _Nobelprisen_) are awarded annually by the [Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Swedish_Academy_of_Sciences "Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences"), the [Swedish Academy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swedish_Academy "Swedish Academy"), the [Karolinska Institutet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karolinska_Institute "Karolinska Institute"), and the [Norwegian Nobel Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norwegian_Nobel_Committee "Norwegian Nobel Committee") to individuals and organizations who make outstanding contributions in the fields of [chemistry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize_in_Chemistry "Nobel Prize in Chemistry"), [physics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize_in_Physics "Nobel Prize in Physics"), [literature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize_in_Literature "Nobel Prize in Literature"), [peace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Peace_Prize "Nobel Peace Prize"), and [physiology or medicine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize_in_Physiology_or_Medicine "Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Nobel_laureates#cite_note-1) They were established by the 1895 will of [Alfred Nobel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alfred_Nobel "Alfred Nobel"), which dictates that the awards should be administered by the [Nobel Foundation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Foundation "Nobel Foundation"). An additional prize in memory of Alfred Nobel was established in 1968 by [Sveriges Riksbank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sveriges_Riksbank "Sveriges Riksbank") (Sweden's [central bank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_bank "Central bank")) for outstanding contributions to the field of [economics](https://en.wikipedia.or... [truncated]

199|## Prize
200|
201|Different organisations are responsible for awarding the individual prizes; the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences awards the Prizes in Physics, Chemistry, and Economics; the Swedish Academy awards the Prize in Literature; the Karolinska Institute awards the Prize in Physiology or Medicine; and the Norwegian Nobel Committee awards the Prize in Peace.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Nobel_laureates#cite_note-3) Each recipient receives a medal, a diploma and a monetary award that has varied throughout the years.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Nobel_laureates#cite_note-NobelPrizeDescription-2) In 1901, the recipients of the first Nobel Prizes were given 150,782 [SEK](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swedish_krona "Swedish krona"), equivalent to 10.8 million SEK in 2023. In 2017, the laureates were awarded a prize amount of 9 million SEK.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Nobel_laureates#cite_note-4) The awards are presented in [Stockholm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stockholm "Stockholm") in an annual ceremony on December 10, the anniversary of Nobel's death.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Nobel_laureates#cite_note-5)
202|
203|In years in which the Nobel Prize is not awarded due to external events or a lack of nominations, the prize money is returned to the funds delegated to the relevant prize.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Nobel_laureates#cite_note-Winners1942-6) The Nobel Prize was not awarded between 1940 and 1942 due to the outbreak of [World War II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II "World War II").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Nobel_laureates#cite_note-PeacePrizeArticle-7)

205|## Laureates
206|
207|Between 1901 and 2017, the [Nobel Prizes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prizes "Nobel Prizes") and the [Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Memorial_Prize_in_Economic_Sciences "Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences") were awarded 585 times to 923 people and organizations. With some receiving the Nobel Prize more than once, this makes a total of 892 individuals (including 844 men, 48 women) and 24 organizations.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Nobel_laureates#cite_note-8) Six Nobel laureates were not permitted by their governments to accept the Nobel Prize. [Adolf Hitler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adolf_Hitler "Adolf Hitler") forbade four Germans, [Richard Kuhn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Kuhn "Richard Kuhn") (Chemistry, 1938), [Adolf Butenandt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adolf_Butenandt "Adolf Butenandt") (Chemistry, 1939), [Gerhard Domagk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gerhard_Domagk "Gerhard Domagk") (Physiology or Medicine, 1939) and [Carl von Ossietzky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carl_von_Ossietzky "Carl von Ossietzky") (Peace, 1936) from accepting their Nobel Prizes. The [Chinese government](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Government_of_China "Government of China") forbade [Liu Xiaobo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liu_Xiaobo "Liu Xiaobo") from accepting his Nobel Prize (Peace, 2010)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Nobel_laureates#cite_note-9) and the government of the [Soviet Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soviet_Union "Soviet Union") pressured [Boris Pasternak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Pasternak "Boris Pasternak") (Literature, 1958) to decline his award. [Liu Xiaobo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liu_Xiaobo "Liu Xiaobo"), [Carl von Ossietzky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carl_von_Ossietzky "Carl von Ossietzky") and [Aung San Suu Kyi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aung_San_Suu_Kyi "Aung San Suu Kyi") were all awarded their Nobel Prize while in prison... [truncated]
208|
209|Seven laureates have received more than one prize; of the seven, the [International Committee of the Red Cross](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Committee_of_the_Red_Cross "International Committee of the Red Cross") has received the [Nobel Peace Prize](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Peace_Prize "Nobel Peace Prize") three times, more than any other.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Nobel_laureates#cite_note-NobelFacts-11)[UNHCR](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UNHCR "UNHCR") (United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees) has been awarded the [Nobel Peace Prize](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Peace_Prize "Nobel Peace Prize") twice. Also the [Nobel Prize in Physics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize_in_Physics "Nobel Prize in Physics") was awarded to [John Bardeen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Bardeen "John Bardeen") twice, as was the [Nobel Prize in Chemistry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize_in_Chemistry "Nobel Prize in Chemistry") to [Frederick Sanger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frederick_Sanger "Frederick Sanger") and [Karl Barry Sharpless](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karl_Barry_Sharpless "Karl Barry Sharpless"). Two laureates have been awarded twice but not in the same field: [Marie Curie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marie_Curie "Marie Curie") (Physics and Chemistry) and [Linus Pauling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Linus_Pauling "Linus Pauling") (Chemistry and Peace). Among the 892 Nobel laureates, 48 have been women; the first woman to receive a Nobel Prize was [Marie Curie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marie_Curie "Marie Curie"), who received the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1903.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Nobel_laureates#cite_note-WomenLaureates-12) She was also the first person (male or female) to be awarded two Nobel Prizes, the second award being the Nobel Prize in Chemistry, given in 1911.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Nobel_laureates#cite_note-NobelFacts-11)

356|## 50-year secrecy rule
357|
358|The Committee neither informs the media nor the candidates themselves of the names of the nominees. Insofar as specific names frequently appear in the early predictions of who will receive the award in any given year, this is either pure speculation or inside information from the person or people who submitted the nomination. After fifty years, the database of nominations maintained by the Nobel Committee is made available to the public.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Nobel_laureates#cite_note-25) Statutes of the Nobel Foundation, § 10, states:
359|
360|> A prize-awarding body may, however, after due consideration in each individual case, permit access to material which formed the basis for the evaluation and decision concerning a prize, for purposes of research in intellectual history. Such permission may not, however, be granted until at least 50 years have elapsed after the date on which the decision in question was made.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Nobel_laureates#cite_note-26)

Complete list of Nobel laureates from 1901–2009 across all six categories: Physics, Chemistry, Physiology or Medicine, Literature, Peace, and Economic Sciences (from 1969).

- **Total years**: 109 (1901–2009, excluding 1940–1942 WWII cancellations)
- **Categories**: 6 (Economic Sciences added 1969)
- **Total awards**: ~585 prizes awarded to ~923 individuals/organizations

{"content": "150|**Robert & Ethel Kennedy Human Rights Center** (formerly the "Robert F. Kennedy Human Rights" and **Robert F. Kennedy Center for Justice and Human Rights**, or **RFK Center**)[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Human_Rights#cite_note-introducing-1) is an American [501(c)(3)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/501(c)(3)_organization "501(c)(3) organization") nonprofit [human rights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_rights "Human rights")[advocacy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Advocacy "Advocacy") organization.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Human_Rights#cite_note-rfkcen-2)[_[better source needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Verifiability#Questionable\_sources "Wikipedia:Verifiability")_] It was named after [United States Senator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Senate "U.S. Senate")[Robert F. Kennedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy "Robert F. Kennedy") in 1968, a few months after [his assassination](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assassination_of_Robert_F._Kennedy "Assassination of Robert F. Kennedy"). The organization of leading attorneys, advocates, entrepreneurs and writers is dedicated to a more just and peaceful world, working alongside local activists to ensure lasting positive change in governments and corporations. It also promotes human rights advocacy through its [RFK Human Rights Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Human_Rights#Human_Rights_Advocacy_and_Award), and supports [investigative journalists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Investigative_journalism "Investigative journalism") and authors through the [RFK Book and Journalism Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Human_Rights#Book_Award). It is based in New York and [Washington, D.C.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington,_D.C. "Washington, D.C.")[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Human_Rights#cite_note-3) Robert F. Kennedy's daughter, [Kerry Kennedy](https://en.wikipedia.or... [truncated]
151|
152|## History
153|
154|[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Robert_F._Kennedy_Human_Rights&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]
155|
156|The Robert F. Kennedy Memorial was originally established as a [non-profit organization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-profit_organization "Non-profit organization") in Washington, D.C., in October, 1968. The [Kennedy family](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kennedy_family "Kennedy family") and friends looked to memorialize Robert Kennedy's public service following [his assassination](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assassination_of_Robert_F._Kennedy "Assassination of Robert F. Kennedy") on June 5, 1968, in [Los Angeles, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles,_California "Los Angeles, California"). [Fred Dutton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fred_Dutton "Fred Dutton"), a long-time friend and Kennedy ally, was named executive director, and [Peter B. Edelman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_B._Edelman "Peter B. Edelman"), a member of Kennedy's senatorial staff, became associate director. The chairman of the executive committee was former U.S. Secretary of Defense [Robert S. McNamara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_S._McNamara "Robert S. McNamara").[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]
157|
158|The Memorial was announced during a press conference at [Hickory Hill in McLean, Virginia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hickory_Hill_(McLean,_Virginia) "Hickory Hill (McLean, Virginia)"), on Tuesday, October 29, 1968. Kennedy's brother [Ted](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_Kennedy "Ted Kennedy") led the press conference, stating that the organization would be a "living memorial" that would work in areas of poverty, crime, and education in America. He went on to say the Memorial would be "an action-oriented program that we think will carry on his concerns, his actions, his efforts to work on so many of the problems in this country that have no solutions". He was joined at the press conference by his sisters, [Patricia Kennedy Lawford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patricia_Kennedy_Lawford "Patricia Kennedy Lawford") and [Jean Kennedy Smith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jean_Kennedy_Smith "Jean Kennedy Smith"), as well as dozens of Kennedy family friends and aides.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Human_Rights#cite_note-4)
159|
160|Kennedy's widow [Ethel Kennedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethel_Kennedy "Ethel Kennedy") did not attend the press conference, but was nearby, in a second-floor bedroom of Hickory Hill on doctor's orders, awaiting the birth of her eleventh child. She issued a statement saying it was the hope of her husband's family and friends that the Robert F. Kennedy Memorial would carry forward the ideals he worked for during his lifetime: "He wanted to encourage the young people and to help the disadvantaged and discriminated against both here and abroad, and he wanted to promote peace in the world. These will be the goals of the memorial."[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Human_Rights#cite_note-5)
161|
162|The memorial and other projects started in Kennedy's memory were later collectively renamed Robert F. Kennedy Human Rights.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Human_Rights#cite_note-6)[_[better source needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Verifiability#Questionable\_sources "Wikipedia:Verifiability")_]
163|
164|## Awards
165|
166|[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Robert_F._Kennedy_Human_Rights&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Awards")]

168|### Human Rights Award
169|
170|[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Robert_F._Kennedy_Human_Rights&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Human Rights Award")]
171|
172|The Robert F. Kennedy Human Rights Award was created by [Kathleen Kennedy Townsend](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kathleen_Kennedy_Townsend "Kathleen Kennedy Townsend") in 1984 to honor individuals around the world who show courage and have made a significant contribution to [human rights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_rights "Human rights") in their country.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]
173|
174|In addition to receiving a financial award, laureates can partner with the RFK Center on projects to advance their human rights work, benefiting from the resources and technologies at the foundation's disposal. Some have achieved their goals, some are in exile from their home country. The majority continue to live in their home country and work with the support of the center to establish the human rights they are working for.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]
175|
176|Since 1984, awards have been given to 43 individuals and organizations from 25 different countries.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] The 2009 award was presented by [President](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_the_United_States "President of the United States")[Barack Obama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama "Barack Obama").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Human_Rights#cite_note-7) In 2009, the RFK Human Rights began a partnership with the [California International Law Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California_International_Law_Center "California International Law Center") (CILC) at the [University of California, Davis School of Law](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Davis_School_of_Law "University of California, Davis School of Law") focusing on the crisis in [Darfur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Darfur "Darfur").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Human_Rights#cite_note-8)[_[better source needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Verifiability#Questionable\_sources "Wikipedia:Verifiability")_]

248|### Ripple of Hope Award
249|
250|[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Robert_F._Kennedy_Human_Rights&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Ripple of Hope Award")]
251|
252|Each year, the Robert F. Kennedy Ripple of Hope Award honors exemplary leaders across [government](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Government "Government"), [business](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Business "Business"), [advocacy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Advocacy "Advocacy"), and [entertainment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Entertainment "Entertainment") who have demonstrated an unwavering commitment to [social change](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Social_change "Social change") and worked to protect and advance [equity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Equity_(law) "Equity (law)"), [justice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justice "Justice"), and [human rights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_rights "Human rights").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Human_Rights#cite_note-14) The name of the award is inspired by Kennedy's [Ripple of Hope speech](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ripple_of_Hope_speech "Ripple of Hope speech") in 1966.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Human_Rights#cite_note-15)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Human_Rights#cite_note-ripple2020-16) They first presented the award in 2007.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Human_Rights#cite_note-:0-17)

283|### Book Award

285|[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Robert_F._Kennedy_Human_Rights&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Book Award")]

287|The Robert F. Kennedy Book Award was founded in 1980, with the proceeds from [Arthur Schlesinger, Jr.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthur_Schlesinger,_Jr. "Arthur Schlesinger, Jr.")'s biography, _Robert Kennedy and His Times_. Each year, the organization presents an award to the book which "most faithfully and forcefully reflects Robert Kennedy's purposes – his concern for the poor and the powerless, his struggle for honest and even-handed justice, his conviction that a decent society must assure all young people a fair chance, and his faith that a free democracy can act to remedy disparities of power and opportunity."[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Human_Rights#cite_note-25)[_[better source needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Verifiability#Questionable\_sources "Wikipedia:Verifiability")_]

340|### Journalism Award
341|
342|[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Robert_F._Kennedy_Human_Rights&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Journalism Award")]
343|
344|Main article: [Robert F. Kennedy Journalism Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Journalism_Award "Robert F. Kennedy Journalism Award")
345|
346|The Robert F. Kennedy Journalism Award was established in 1968 by a group of reporters covering Kennedy's presidential campaign and "honors those who report on issues that reflect Kennedy's concerns including human rights, social justice and the power of individual action in the United States and around the world."[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Human_Rights#cite_note-27)[_[better source needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Verifiability#Questionable\_sources "Wikipedia:Verifiability")_] Entries include insights into the causes, conditions and remedies of injustice and critical analysis of relevant public policies, programs, attitudes and private endeavors.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]
347|
348|Led by a committee of six independent journalists, the Awards are judged by more than fifty journalists each year. Previous winners include [World News](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ABC_World_News "ABC World News") anchor [Diane Sawyer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diane_Sawyer "Diane Sawyer").
